summary: TechCrunch's Morgan Sung argues that Republicans still fail to connect with young voters online, using Vivek Ramaswamy's trolled TikTok debut and Jake Paul endorsement as the main example. Democrats such as Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and John Fetterman set the digital blueprint through platform-native authenticity, while Republican efforts like Matt Gaetz's Twitch stream and Ron DeSantis's Twitter Spaces launch flopped. Experts quoted say authenticity and creator mobilization matter more than endorsements, and that unpopular policies toward Gen Z are a further obstacle.
one_line: Republican candidates like Vivek Ramaswamy keep flopping on TikTok and Twitch because they lack platform fluency and authenticity, while Democrats lead digital strategy.
key_facts: Vivek Ramaswamy launched his TikTok presence with an endorsement from Jake Paul, even though he proposed raising the voting age to 25 (unless people serve in the military or pass a civics exam).
Ramaswamy's TikTok account gained over 50,000 followers within weeks, but his comments are flooded with sex jokes (mainly about edging) and trolling, including hexes from witchtok creators.
Ramaswamy previously called TikTok "digital fentanyl" from China, which conflicts with his decision to join the platform.

A 2022 midterm report by the Alliance for Securing Democracy found 47% of Democratic Senate candidates had TikTok accounts versus 12% of Republican candidates; for House candidates it was 30% of Democrats versus 10% of Republicans.
Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez's 2020 "Among Us" Twitch stream with Pokimane, Hasan Piker, Corpse Husband and Mxmtoon was one of the most viewed streams in the site's history.
Matt Gaetz's Twitch debut was a 30-minute diatribe about the January 6 Capitol riot with Darren Beattie, peaked at six live viewers, and his open chat was bombarded with ASCII art.

A 2023 paper in the International Journal of Communication, co-authored by Martin Riedl, found mobilizing influencers is more effective than using their endorsements, because blatant endorsements create an "authenticity gap."
Annie Wu Henry, the strategist behind Fetterman's TikTok success, says Gen Z "does not put up with bullshit" and that it's hard to sell policies that attack the generation.
North Carolina Rep. Jeff Jackson has over 2.2 million TikTok followers using plain explanatory videos without internet humor.

The Biden team is building an "army of influencers," but paid undisclosed political influencing is legally murky; the conservative agency Influenceable recruited Gen Z creators without disclosing pay.
Ron DeSantis launched his presidential campaign in May on Twitter Spaces with Elon Musk; technical issues ended it after 21 minutes.

Gen Z activists have trolled conservative efforts, including empty seats at a 2020 Trump rally, Shrek porn on a Texas anti-abortion tip form, and fanfiction on the Missouri attorney general's tip form.
